Apple is exploring a new option that could wipe an iPhone's storage more thoroughly when you erase the device — but with a catch. Here are the details.

China-exclusive new feature

Code references found in today's iOS 27.2 beta 1 release indicate that iPhones will gain a new erase option that allows users to completely overwrite the device's entire storage — including the inactive portion — with blank data.

In addition to wiping the iPhone's data, this feature overwrites the device's entire storage — including the inactive portion — with blank data. Apple warns that this process may take longer than a standard erase and could affect the device's lifespan.

This is an interesting move, as currently when users erase an iPhone, the device's encryption key is destroyed, making the remaining data effectively unreadable. Apple actually makes this clear in an Apple Platform Deployment support document:

9to5Mac confirmed after checking today's beta version that, in its current implementation, this feature will only be available on iPhone models sold in China — Apple appears to be adding this feature to comply with an upcoming data erasure regulation.

This is because a new Chinese standard taking effect on January 1, 2027 will require smartphones and other electronic devices to provide more thorough methods for clearing stored data, including by means of overwriting.

For semiconductor storage (such as the flash storage used in smartphones), one of the approved methods is to overwrite the storage space containing user data with meaningless data at least once. This aligns closely with Apple's described approach of replacing the storage space with blank data.

Finally, this new erase option is not exclusive to iPhone — code references also indicate it will support other devices, including iPad, HomePod, and Apple Vision Pro.
